By Mike Allen · Nov 20, 2026

🥳 Happy Friday! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 538 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Amy Stern for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Anthropic slumps amid tech sell-off
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Anthropic shares are slumping in their first full trading day, while the S&P 500 flirts with correction territory, Axios' Nathan Bomey reports.

  • The Claude maker was seen as a catalyst that could prop up the AI economy. But its record-setting IPO arrived just as investors were losing faith in the emerging tech and the huge spending supporting it.

By the numbers: Anthropic shares were down about 10% as of midafternoon, trading at about $87.

  • That's far below yesterday's opening price ($111.50) and their all-time high ($115.10).

🖼️ The big picture: Anthropic's downturn coincides with a significant drop-off for chips supplier Nvidia, which has now lost more than $1.6 trillion in market cap from its all-time high.

  • Nvidia is grappling with the fallout from the Jensen Huang scandal, plus fears over unsustainable AI spending.

Other AI-linked stocks are also struggling, with the Nasdaq down 4.3% as of midafternoon.

  • Tech analyst Dan Ives wrote: "This is a painful tech sell-off."

👀 What we're watching: The broader S&P 500 was down about 2.8%.

  • Closing there would leave it more than 10% below its 52-week high — the textbook definition of a market correction. Go deeper.

🧮 Meanwhile: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims to have solved math's most infamous unsolved problem — with Claude's help.

  • The Wall Street Journal reports: "If the proof checks out, it would count as the most remarkable accomplishment in the year of AI's extraordinary math progress." Go deeper (gift link).
 
 
2. 📈 Consumer sentiment surges
 
Data: University of Michigan; Chart: Neil Irwin/Axios

Consumer sentiment popped this month amid the midterm elections and a moderation in energy prices, Axios' Neil Irwin reports.

🖼️ The big picture: Sentiment remains below its pre-Iran war levels, but Americans feel better about their personal finances.

  • They also view the soon-to-be divided government as better for their pocketbooks.

📈 By the numbers: The University of Michigan's overall consumer sentiment index was 51.5 in November, up from 48 in October.

  • That 7.3% rise was fueled by a strong gain in expectations for the future.

4. 🌺 1 for the road: Inside the Smithsonian's holiday workshop
 
Over a thousand poinsettias ready for their holiday debut at Smithsonian Gardens. Photo: Anna Spiegel/Axios

Axios D.C.'s Anna Spiegel recently got a rare behind-the-scenes tour of Smithsonian Gardens' greenhouses in Suitland, Maryland.

🎄 Christmas starts in April at the Smithsonian, when the team orders poinsettias for the coming holidays.

  • Tiny rooted cuttings arrive around the Fourth of July. Over the next five months, they're watered, fertilized and pruned into showstoppers.
  • Come September, it's lights out: Poinsettias need more than 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness to develop.
Horticulturalist Jill Gonzalez hand-ties each poinsettia. Photo: Anna Spiegel/Axios

Each museum gets its own holiday look.

  • Air and Space goes for celestial themes, while Natural History favors pink poinsettias. American History? Classic Christmas red.
